Answer: B
Reason: Scimitar syndrome is characterized by partial anomalous pulmonary venous return from the right lung to the IVC, creating a curvilinear "scimitar" shadow on CXR, and is frequently associated with right lung hypoplasia (often involving the upper lobe) and dextroposition of the heart. Option B correctly identifies these key features (right-sided opacity/hypoplasia and dextroposition), whereas the other options describe findings inconsistent with this congenital anomaly.
